tasks.short: Oversee life-cycle assessments and identify environmental improvements across products, processes and distribution.

steps.what: Agree assessment boundaries, functional unit, allocation methods and intended use.
Export material quantities, energy use, transport movements and waste records.
Request and collect supplier and provider environmental records.
Read environmental evidence and map quantities, units and coverage into the assessment inventory.

loop.input: Environmental evidence and activity extract, with the approved assessment scope.
loop.output: Proposed inventory mappings with source passages, units, periods and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate units, totals, duplicate records and source references; the specialist approves ambiguous mappings.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document. Missing or conflicting fields go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express quantities and assessment boundaries in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Calculate impacts in {OTHER} life-cycle assessment software using mapped inventory and selected factors.
Interpret hotspots, uncertainty and sensitivity; prepare the assessment report.

loop.input: Validated impact and sensitivity results, assessment scope and evidence gaps.
loop.output: Report draft with cited results, limitations and candidate improvement options.
loop.check: Bind numerical tables to calculated results. The specialist checks interpretation and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision. Unresolved methodological issues require specialist writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables can be templated, but explaining uncertainty and tradeoffs requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Accept the assessment and select improvements for operational planning.

tasks.design: An integration on {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers activity records from {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, while configured {WORKFLOW} requests collect environmental evidence through {PARTNER_PORTAL}. A bounded loop proposes evidence mappings, configured {OTHER} life-cycle assessment software calculates impacts, and a second bounded loop drafts a source-linked report in {DOCS}; specialists approve methods and interpretation before the manager selects improvements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activity records, supplier evidence and assessment models were disconnected. Integrations required bespoke work, while boundaries and allocation still required specialist judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance makes connectors, validation rules and report templates cheaper to build. Bounded extraction can reduce document handling; assessment methods and factor quality still need expert review.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete supplier data, factor licensing, allocation choices and comparable system boundaries. External comparative claims may require additional independent review.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible boundaries and distinguish a real improvement from an impact shifted elsewhere.

ambition.what: Compare packaging alternatives before each scheduled product redesign.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing inputs and assembling reports, and more time evaluating operational tradeoffs. Existing approval rights remain; any new packaging decision authority must be delegated.

reach.task: Model transport and packaging scenarios using consistent activity units.
reach.learn: Functional units, allocation methods, factor provenance and sensitivity analysis.

reach.task: Trace assessment conclusions to controlled operating records.
reach.learn: Evidence lineage, uncertainty documentation and assessment review criteria.

evidence.claim: Structured activity calculations and integrations can be deterministic; boundary choices and interpretation need specialists.
Standard life-cycle assessment software can calculate impacts from an inventory and selected factors.
The digest contains no documented life-cycle assessment automation case supporting this design or its time estimates.

assumptions: The manager oversees a sustainability specialist or external assessor rather than performing every calculation.
Configured {OTHER} life-cycle assessment software and licensed impact factors are available.
Automatic requests use approved templates, recipients and reminder limits.
The structured-input prior fits calculations; low rule coverage fits methodology and interpretation.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one assessment pilot, excluding supplier waiting time and factor procurement.
Access work includes GDPR checks where records identify people and employee consultation under national rules where applicable. The EU AI Act applies according to intended use.
unknowns: Who owns the assessment method and technical approval?
Which activity records are accessible from {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}?
Which factor datasets and assessment software are licensed?
Are results intended for internal decisions or external comparative claims?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed data access?
research_questions: Which inventory fields can be imported directly into the assessment software?
What document-mapping error rate is acceptable for each inventory category?
Which assessment claims require independent critical review?
new_work: Review proposed evidence mappings and unresolved gaps.
Maintain unit conversions, factor versions and import rules.
Check report interpretations against sensitivity results.
Monitor failed imports, expired evidence and access permissions.

tasks.short: Review storage and distribution providers' carbon footprints and environmental records before qualification or renewal.

steps.what: Identify current providers and candidates due for environmental review.
Agree evidence requirements, comparison boundaries and environmental qualification criteria.
Request footprint reports, environmental certificates and supporting activity records.
Read reports and record emissions, periods, boundaries, assurance and certificate validity.

loop.input: Provider reports, certificates and supporting records.
loop.output: Structured environmental fields with source passages and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Validate units, reporting dates, certificate dates and source references. The analyst reviews ambiguous boundaries.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document. Conflicts or unreadable evidence enter a review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports describe assurance, scope and exclusions in varied free text.

steps.what: Compare provider records using consistent units and flag incompatible coverage.
Discuss missing evidence and methodological differences with providers.
Decide environmental suitability and agree any supplier conditions.
Record the approved assessment, supplier conditions and next review date.

tasks.design: Configured {WORKFLOW} requests collect provider evidence through {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and a bounded extraction loop creates source-linked records from documents in {DOCS}. Deterministic comparisons feed {BI}; the manager resolves methodological differences with providers, and approved assessments and conditions are recorded in {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports used different units, periods and boundaries. Evidence chasing and manual comparison offered little reusable structure between annual reviews.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable requests, document extraction and cheaper integration code can maintain a reusable evidence record. Transparent comparability checks reduce preparation without claiming that every footprint is comparable.
tasks.still_hard: Unverified provider claims, missing subcontractor emissions and different allocation methods. A low reported footprint may reflect incomplete coverage rather than better performance.
tasks.human_edge: Judge evidence credibility and negotiate achievable improvements without rewarding weak disclosure.

ambition.what: Offer environmental evidence packs for customer logistics tenders.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less review time collecting reports and more time discussing evidence quality and improvement commitments. Supplier qualification rights remain with existing approvers; releasing customer evidence packs needs an agreed mandate.

reach.task: Compare provider emissions intensity for equivalent transport and storage services.
reach.learn: Comparable denominators, reporting boundaries, assurance levels and allocation methods.

reach.task: Maintain traceable provider evidence and investigate unsupported environmental claims.
reach.learn: Certificate scope, validity checks and evidence-based corrective actions.

evidence.claim: Configured requests and deterministic comparisons can reduce collection and spreadsheet preparation.
Document extraction needs source checks; environmental suitability still depends on judgement and comparable boundaries.
The digest contains no provider environmental-record review case establishing this design's savings.

assumptions: A recurring provider review uses existing supplier records and approved evidence requirements.
Requests and reminders use approved templates and recipient lists.
The gathering-heavy prior fits this task, but provider clarification remains a distinct human conversation.
The mail-share prior understates collection where providers lack a common portal.
No automatic supplier rejection follows a missing field or comparison flag.
Build ranges cover one provider-review pilot in working days and exclude provider response delays.
Access work includes GDPR checks for named contacts and employee consultation under national rules where applicable. EU AI Act applicability depends on intended use.
unknowns: How many providers are reviewed, and which evidence formats do they supply?
Does {PROCUREMENT} support environmental fields, approval records and renewal reminders?
Who may approve environmental qualification and communicate supplier conditions?
Which customer requirements determine reporting boundaries and assurance expectations?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed data access?
research_questions: Which comparison rules reliably distinguish comparable records from incompatible coverage?
Can certificate validity be checked against authoritative issuer records?
What evidence may be reused in customer tenders under provider confidentiality terms?
new_work: Review extraction exceptions and unsupported provider claims.
Maintain comparison rules and evidence requirements.
Track expired certificates and overdue provider responses.
Review customer evidence packs before release.

role.altitude: The supply chain manager gains time for environmental tradeoffs, provider discussions and improvement planning. New decision rights require explicit delegation; faster preparation alone does not expand authority.
reach: Logistics analyst: build comparable environmental scenarios from operating data.
Quality control systems manager: maintain evidence traceability and investigate weak claims.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring environmental decision service that compares packaging and logistics options before commitments and supplies approved evidence for customer tenders.
